html:
The Kriol, or Creoles, are an Afro-Caribbean people of the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua, centred on Bluefields and the Pearl Lagoon. They speak Miskito Coast Creole, an English based creole language.

They did not exist in 1492, when this coast belonged to Indigenous peoples such as the Rama. The Creoles formed in the 1700s and 1800s from Africans brought as slaves by British settlers on the Mosquito Coast, from free Black migrants from Jamaica and other islands, and from British and Indigenous ancestors. Under the British protectorate of the Mosquito Coast they became the educated elite of the region, largely Moravian Protestants. The coast was joined to Nicaragua in 1894, and its Creole and Miskito peoples won a measure of self-rule under the autonomy law of 1987.
